learn.rule: A complete sentence has a subject (who or what) and a predicate (what happens), and together they express a whole idea.
learn.ruleEs: Una oración completa tiene un sujeto (quién o qué) y un predicado (qué sucede), y juntos expresan una idea completa.
learn.model: Decomposers break down dead plants and return nutrients to the soil.
learn.notice: Find the subject (decomposers) and what it does (break down, return). Together they make a whole idea.

items.prompt: Which group of words about an ecosystem is a complete sentence?

options.text: Because the forest canopy blocks most of the sunlight.
Decomposers recycle nutrients back into the soil.
The bacteria living in the soil of the rainforest.

items.why: This one has a subject (decomposers) and a verb (recycle), so it is a whole idea. The others leave the reader waiting for the rest.
items.whyEs: Esta tiene sujeto (decomposers) y verbo (recycle), así que es una idea completa. Las otras dejan al lector esperando el resto.

items.prompt: The words in the box are a fragment. What is missing?
items.text: The tall grasses growing across the open savanna.

options.text: A subject that names who or what
Nothing; it is already a complete sentence
A predicate that tells what the grasses do

items.why: The subject is there (the tall grasses), but we never learn what the grasses do. A fragment is missing its predicate or its subject.
items.whyEs: El sujeto está (the tall grasses), pero nunca sabemos qué hacen. A un fragmento le falta el predicado o el sujeto.

items.prompt: Which choice fixes the run-on sentence?
items.text: Ecosystems depend on balance when one species disappears the whole food web can change.

options.text: Ecosystems depend on balance, when one species disappears the whole food web can change.
Ecosystems depend on balance. When one species disappears, the whole food web can change.
Ecosystems depend on balance when one species disappears, the whole food web can change.

items.why: A run-on jams two ideas together. Split them into two sentences, and put a comma after the opening When clause.
items.whyEs: Una oración corrida junta dos ideas sin separarlas. Sepáralas en dos oraciones y pon una coma después de la cláusula con When.

items.prompt: Choose the words that finish the sentence.
parts: Although the pond froze solid in January,

options: and the fish beneath the ice.
since the fish beneath the ice.
the fish survived beneath the ice.
parts.answer: the fish survived beneath the ice.

items.model: Although the pond froze solid in January, the fish survived beneath the ice.
items.why: The opening clause with Although needs a whole idea to follow it. Only the last choice has a subject and a verb (the fish survived).
items.whyEs: La cláusula con Although necesita una idea completa después. Solo la última opción tiene sujeto y verbo (the fish survived).

items.prompt: Check every complete sentence about ecosystems.

options.text: Photosynthesis converts sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into sugar.
Such as owls, hawks, and other birds of prey.
Running through the dense understory of the jungle.
Energy flows from the sun to producers and then to consumers.
When the predator population declined.

items.why: Each complete sentence names who or what and says what happens. The fragments are missing a main verb or begin a thought they never finish.
items.whyEs: Cada oración completa dice quién o qué y qué sucede. A los fragmentos les falta un verbo principal o empiezan una idea que no terminan.

items.prompt: Which group of words is a fragment?

options.text: Deer eat the tender shoots of young trees.
Because the wetland filters pollutants from the water.
Snakes, frogs, and lizards live in the wetland.

items.why: Because makes the reader expect a result, but the sentence stops. A because clause cannot stand alone.
items.whyEs: Because hace esperar un resultado, pero la oración se detiene. Una cláusula con because no puede estar sola.

write.prompt: Write one complete sentence about how living things depend on each other in an ecosystem.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración completa sobre cómo los seres vivos dependen unos de otros en un ecosistema.
write.text: Topic: how living things depend on each other

label: I started with a capital letter
Empecé con mayúscula

write.model: In a healthy ecosystem, plants make food from sunlight and animals depend on those plants for energy.

familyTalk.en: Name a place you know, like a park or pond. Say one whole sentence about what lives there and what it needs.
familyTalk.es: Elijan un lugar que conozcan, como un parque o un estanque. Digan una oración completa sobre lo que vive ahí y lo que necesita.

teacherTip.en: Have students underline the subject once and the predicate twice in each complete sentence before they tackle the fragments.
teacherTip.es: Pide que subrayen el sujeto una vez y el predicado dos veces en cada oración completa antes de trabajar con los fragmentos.

sets.title: Traders on the Silk Road
sets.titleEs: Los comerciantes de la Ruta de la Seda

learn.rule: Check every sentence for a subject and a verb, and make sure the idea is finished. If the reader is left waiting, it is a fragment.
learn.ruleEs: Revisa que cada oración tenga sujeto y verbo, y que la idea esté terminada. Si el lector queda esperando, es un fragmento.
learn.model: Merchants carried silk and spices along the Silk Road for more than a thousand years.
learn.notice: Ask two questions: Who or what? What happened? If both are answered, the idea is whole.

items.prompt: Which group of words about trade routes is a complete sentence?

options.text: Camel caravans crossing the Taklamakan Desert in the summer heat.
Which spread new ideas as well as goods along the routes.
Traders exchanged silk, paper, and spices for horses and glass.

items.why: Only the last choice tells who did something (traders) and what they did (exchanged). The others describe or add on without finishing an idea.
items.whyEs: Solo la última dice quién hizo algo (traders) y qué hizo (exchanged). Las otras describen o agregan sin terminar una idea.

items.prompt: Which choice turns the fragment into a complete sentence?
items.text: The Mongol Empire, which stretched from China to Eastern Europe.

options.text: The Mongol Empire, which stretched from China to Eastern Europe, protected trade along the Silk Road.
The Mongol Empire, which stretched from China to Eastern Europe and included many busy trade cities along the way.
Which stretched from China to Eastern Europe, the Mongol Empire.

items.why: The original has a subject but no main verb. Adding protected trade gives the empire something to do, so the idea is whole.
items.whyEs: La original tiene sujeto pero no verbo principal. Al agregar protected trade, el imperio hace algo y la idea queda completa.

items.prompt: Which choice correctly fixes the run-on about silk?
items.text: Silk was valuable in Rome many Romans paid high prices for it.

options.text: Silk was valuable in Rome, many Romans paid high prices for it.
Silk was valuable in Rome, so many Romans paid high prices for it.
Silk was valuable in Rome many Romans, paid high prices for it.

items.why: Two complete ideas need more than a comma. A comma plus a joining word like so fixes the run-on and shows the result.
items.whyEs: Dos ideas completas necesitan más que una coma. Una coma más una palabra de unión como so arregla la oración corrida y muestra el resultado.

items.prompt: Choose the verb form that completes the Marco Polo sentence.
parts: from Venice to the court of Kublai Khan in the thirteenth century.
items.model: Marco Polo traveled from Venice to the court of Kublai Khan in the thirteenth century.
items.why: A sentence needs a verb that works as the main verb. Traveling and to travel cannot do that job by themselves.
items.whyEs: Una oración necesita un verbo que funcione como verbo principal. Traveling y to travel no pueden hacerlo solos.

items.prompt: Check every complete sentence about the Silk Road.

options.text: Ibn Battuta journeyed across Africa, Asia, and Europe for nearly thirty years.
After the caravan reached the oasis at dusk.
Merchants rested at caravanserais, which were roadside inns.
The shimmering silk and the rare spices from distant lands.
Whether the journey would be safe or dangerous.

items.why: The two complete sentences each finish an idea. The others start a thought (After, Whether) or name things without saying what happened.
items.whyEs: Las dos oraciones completas terminan una idea. Las otras empiezan un pensamiento (After, Whether) o nombran cosas sin decir qué pasó.

items.prompt: The second group of words in the box is a fragment. How should the writer fix it?
items.text: Along the Silk Road, many cities grew wealthy from trade. Such as Samarkand and Chang'an.

options.text: Add a question mark after Chang'an.
Join it to the first sentence with a comma.
Start it with a lowercase letter and keep the period.

items.why: Such as Samarkand and Chang'an gives examples of the cities, so it belongs inside the first sentence: ...from trade, such as Samarkand and Chang'an.
items.whyEs: Such as Samarkand and Chang'an da ejemplos de las ciudades, así que va dentro de la primera oración: ...from trade, such as Samarkand and Chang'an.

write.prompt: Write one complete sentence that tells what traders carried along the Silk Road or why the road mattered.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración completa que diga qué llevaban los comerciantes por la Ruta de la Seda o por qué era importante.

label: I started with a capital letter
Empecé con mayúscula

write.model: Along the Silk Road, traders carried silk, spices, and new ideas between China and the Mediterranean.

familyTalk.en: Ask your student to tell you one fact about trade or travel long ago, in a whole sentence with who and what happened.
familyTalk.es: Pidan a su estudiante que cuente un dato sobre el comercio o los viajes de hace mucho tiempo, en una oración completa que diga quién y qué pasó.

teacherTip.en: Post two sentence-checking questions (Who or what? What happened?) and have students say them aloud for each example.
teacherTip.es: Muestra dos preguntas para revisar oraciones (¿Quién o qué? ¿Qué pasó?) y pide que las digan en voz alta con cada ejemplo.

learn.rule: When you write about a story, every sentence must be a whole idea. A fragment leaves out the subject or the verb, or starts a thought and never finishes it.
learn.ruleEs: Cuando escribes sobre un cuento, cada oración debe ser una idea completa. Un fragmento omite el sujeto o el verbo, o empieza un pensamiento y no lo termina.
learn.model: Nadia climbed the spiral staircase while the storm shook the old lighthouse.
learn.notice: Look for the character (who) and the action (what happened). A whole idea has both.

items.prompt: Which group of words from a story is a complete sentence?

options.text: The old lighthouse on the rocky cliff above the harbor.
Waiting for the storm to pass over the dark water.
Nadia climbed the spiral staircase to the lamp room.

items.why: Nadia is the subject and climbed is the action. The other choices describe a setting or an action without finishing an idea.
items.whyEs: Nadia es el sujeto y climbed es la acción. Las otras opciones describen un lugar o una acción sin terminar una idea.

items.prompt: The story words in the box are a fragment. What do they still need?
items.text: The narrator, remembering the long summer afterward.

options.text: A verb that tells what the narrator did
A subject that names the narrator
A comma after the word narrator

items.why: The subject is there (the narrator), but remembering is not a main verb on its own. We need something like the narrator told the story.
items.whyEs: El sujeto está (the narrator), pero remembering no es un verbo principal por sí solo. Falta algo como the narrator told the story.

items.prompt: Which choice fixes the run-on in the storm scene?
items.text: The storm grew louder Nadia gripped the railing and kept climbing.

options.text: The storm grew louder, Nadia gripped the railing and kept climbing.
The storm grew louder Nadia, gripped the railing and kept climbing.
The storm grew louder, and Nadia gripped the railing and kept climbing.

items.why: There are two complete ideas here. Join them with a comma and the word and, or split them with a period.
items.whyEs: Aquí hay dos ideas completas. Únelas con una coma y la palabra and, o sepáralas con un punto.

items.prompt: Choose the words that finish the lighthouse sentence.
parts: When the beam finally swept across the water,

options: Nadia, who saw the stranded boat.
and Nadia seeing the stranded boat.

items.model: When the beam finally swept across the water, Nadia saw the stranded boat.
items.why: An opening clause with When needs a whole idea after the comma. Only the first choice has a subject and a main verb.
items.whyEs: Una cláusula inicial con When necesita una idea completa después de la coma. Solo la primera opción tiene sujeto y verbo principal.

items.prompt: Check every complete sentence about the story.

options.text: The author describes the setting with vivid sensory details.
Pounding waves and howling wind in the darkness.
Nadia's courage grows as the storm gets worse.
Although the lamp had been dark for ten years.
Which makes the ending feel hopeful.

items.why: The complete sentences each give a subject and say what happens. The fragments are descriptions or dependent clauses that stop too soon.
items.whyEs: Las oraciones completas dan un sujeto y dicen qué sucede. Los fragmentos son descripciones o cláusulas dependientes que se detienen antes.

items.prompt: Which sentence about the story's theme is complete?

options.text: Because Nadia learned that courage can grow during hard moments.
Nadia learns that courage can grow during hard moments.
Nadia, learning that courage can grow during hard moments.

items.why: Because and the -ing form both leave the idea unfinished. Only Nadia learns has a subject and a main verb.
items.whyEs: Because y la forma -ing dejan la idea sin terminar. Solo Nadia learns tiene sujeto y verbo principal.

write.prompt: Write one complete sentence about a character in a story you have read, or about Nadia, and what the character does.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración completa sobre un personaje de un cuento que hayas leído, o sobre Nadia, y lo que hace.
write.text: Topic: a character and an action

label: I started with a capital letter
Empecé con mayúscula

write.model: In the story, Nadia faces her fear and keeps the lighthouse lamp burning through the storm.

familyTalk.en: Tell each other about a movie or book. Use whole sentences: who is in it and what happens?
familyTalk.es: Cuéntense sobre una película o un libro. Usen oraciones completas: ¿quién aparece y qué pasa?

teacherTip.en: Have partners read each item aloud and decide: does it leave me waiting for more? If yes, it is a fragment.
teacherTip.es: Pide que las parejas lean cada ejemplo en voz alta y decidan: ¿me deja esperando más? Si es así, es un fragmento.
